## Benchmarking

```{r}
#| label: bench-setup
#| include: false
# The benchmark functions are installed with the package
# (inst/benchmark/benchmark_functions.R); the same code produced the saved
# timings. The agreement tables below are computed now, at render time,
# from the installed package; the timings are read from the saved results
# of inst/benchmark/benchmark.R, because repeated timing runs would make
# rendering slow and the numbers would change with every render.
library(nbzinbreg)
bench_file <- system.file("benchmark", "benchmark_functions.R",
                          package = "nbzinbreg")
source(bench_file)
specs <- bench_specs()
pairs <- lapply(specs, fit_pair, hessian = "analytic")
bench <- compare_pairs(pairs)
names(bench$tables) <- vapply(specs, `[[`, "", "id")
req <- bench$required

saved_file <- system.file("benchmark", "benchmark_results.rds",
                          package = "nbzinbreg")
saved <- if (nzchar(saved_file)) readRDS(saved_file)
prov_check <- if (!is.null(saved)) check_saved_provenance(saved$provenance)

fmt_est <- function(x) ifelse(is.na(x), "", formatC(x, digits = 7, format = "g"))
fmt_diff <- function(x) ifelse(is.na(x), "", formatC(x, digits = 1, format = "e"))
side_table <- function(id) {
  tab <- bench$tables[[id]]
  out <- data.frame(
    Parameter = tab$parameter,
    Ours = fmt_est(tab$estimate_ours),
    Reference = fmt_est(tab$estimate_reference),
    `|Diff.|` = fmt_diff(tab$estimate_abs_diff),
    `SE ours` = fmt_est(tab$se_ours),
    `SE ref.` = fmt_est(tab$se_reference),
    `SE |diff.|` = fmt_diff(tab$se_abs_diff),
    check.names = FALSE)
  knitr::kable(out, align = "lrrrrrr")
}
max_of <- function(model, quantity) {
  max(req$max_abs_diff[req$model == model & req$quantity == quantity])
}
n_checks <- vapply(bench$validity, nrow, 1L)
all_valid <- all(vapply(bench$validity, pair_valid, logical(1)))
all_passed <- all(req$passed)
ll_higher <- req$note[req$quantity == "log-likelihood"]
```

The package should reproduce the reference implementations: `MASS::glm.nb()`
for the negative binomial (NB) model and `pscl::zeroinfl(dist = "negbin")`
for the zero-inflated negative binomial (ZINB) model. To check this, each
model is fitted to two data sets with both our package and the reference
function, and the two sets of estimates are compared number by number.

**Data and models.** `pscl::bioChemists` (915 biochemistry PhD students;
the response is the number of articles `art`) is modeled with
`fem + mar + kid5 + phd + ment` in the count part and, for ZINB, the same
covariates in the zero part, as in Appendix A of the project description.
`AER::NMES1988` (4,406 people aged 66 and over; the response is the number
of physician office visits `visits`) is modeled with
`hospital + health + chronic + gender + school + insurance` in the count
part and `hospital + chronic + gender + school + insurance` in the zero part.

**Settings.** Our functions run at their **default** settings, which is how
a user would call them. The reference functions run with **tight**
tolerances (`glm.control(epsilon = 1e-10, maxit = 100)` for `glm.nb()` and
`zeroinfl.control(reltol = 1e-12)` for `zeroinfl()`), so that they stop as
close to the exact maximum of the likelihood as they can. Differences then
measure how close our answer is to the exact answer, not the references'
own stopping error.

**What is compared.** For every coefficient, the two estimates and the two
standard errors are shown side by side with their absolute difference
|ours − reference|. The theta row compares theta for NB and log(theta) for
ZINB, the scale on which `zeroinfl()` estimates it; its standard-error
columns hold SE(theta) or SE(log theta). The last row is the maximized
log-likelihood. For each group of numbers the *maximum absolute difference*
is the largest of these absolute differences; the project requires it to
be at most 1e-5 (coefficients and standard errors) and 1e-4 (theta and the
log-likelihood) for NB, and at most 1e-3 for every quantity for ZINB.

**Validity first.** A comparison is only meaningful if both fits are valid.
Before comparing, each pair of fits is checked: both converged (for our
ZINB fit this includes the gradient check at the estimates), all estimates
and standard errors are finite, both fits use the same observations and
the same parameterization (the same coefficient names in the same order),
and both covariance matrices are symmetric and positive definite.
`r if (all_valid) sprintf("All %d checks passed for each of the four pairs.", n_checks[[1]]) else "**Not all checks passed; see the validity tables in the supplementary benchmark article.**"`

```{r}
#| label: tbl-bench-bc-nb
#| tbl-cap: "bioChemists, negative binomial: nbreg() against glm.nb()."
#| echo: false
#| tbl-colwidths: false
side_table("bioChemists_NB")
```

#| label: tbl-bench-nmes-nb
#| tbl-cap: "NMES1988, negative binomial: nbreg() against glm.nb()."
#| echo: false

side_table("NMES1988_NB")

#| label: tbl-bench-bc-zinb

@tbl-bench-summary collects the maximum absolute differences and compares
them with the required tolerances.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-bench-summary
#| tbl-cap: "Maximum absolute differences from the reference fits, against the required tolerances."
#| echo: false
#| tbl-colwidths: false
summ <- data.frame(
  Data = sub("_.*", "", req$pair), Model = req$model, Quantity = req$quantity,
  `Max. abs. difference` = fmt_diff(req$max_abs_diff),
  Tolerance = formatC(req$tolerance, format = "e", digits = 0),
  Met = ifelse(req$passed, "yes", "NO"), check.names = FALSE)
knitr::kable(summ, align = "lllrrc")
```

`r if (all_passed) "Every required quantity is within its tolerance" else "**Not every required quantity is within its tolerance**"`,
with a large margin: the largest differences are
`r fmt_diff(max_of("NB", "coefficients"))` for the NB coefficients and
`r fmt_diff(max_of("ZINB", "coefficients"))` for the ZINB coefficients.
The NB fits agree almost to rounding error, because `nbreg()` and
`glm.nb()` maximize the same likelihood with closely related algorithms
(iteratively reweighted least squares, IRLS, for the coefficients, and a
one-dimensional search for theta). The ZINB differences are larger but
still at least `r floor(1e-3 / max(req$max_abs_diff[req$model == "ZINB"]))`
times below the tolerance: `zinbreg()` stops its EM
algorithm when a gradient check at the estimates passes, which places
every estimate within a tiny fraction of a standard error of the maximum,
while `zeroinfl()` stops its quasi-Newton (BFGS) search by its own
criterion. The log-likelihoods differ by at most
`r fmt_diff(max_of("ZINB", "log-likelihood"))`;
`r if (all(grepl("reference is higher", ll_higher))) "in all four comparisons the reference value is very slightly higher" else "the higher value is reported per pair in the table"`.

**Computation time.** The timings come from the saved results of
`inst/benchmark/benchmark.R`, which runs each fit 10 times with
`bench::mark()` and reports the median and the range. The references are
timed both with the tight settings used above and with their own defaults,
because the tight settings make them slower than in ordinary use.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-bench-time
#| tbl-cap: "Computation time in seconds (median of 10 runs, with the minimum and maximum)."
#| echo: false
#| tbl-colwidths: false
if (is.null(saved)) {
  cat("The saved timings were not found in the installed package; run inst/benchmark/benchmark.R.")
} else {
  tm <- saved$timing
  tm <- tm[!grepl("numeric Hessian", tm$fit), ]
  tm$fit <- sub(", analytic Hessian", "", tm$fit)
  knitr::kable(data.frame(
    Data = tm$data_name, Model = tm$model, Fit = tm$fit,
    `Median (s)` = formatC(tm$median_s, digits = 3, format = "g"),
    `Range (s)` = sprintf("%s to %s", formatC(tm$min_s, digits = 3, format = "g"),
                          formatC(tm$max_s, digits = 3, format = "g")),
    check.names = FALSE), align = "lllrr")
}
```

```{r}
#| label: bench-time-numbers
#| include: false
med <- function(spec, pattern) {
  if (is.null(saved)) return(NA_real_)
  t <- saved$timing
  t$median_s[t$spec == spec & grepl(pattern, t$fit, fixed = TRUE)][1]
}
ratio_bc <- med("bioChemists_ZINB", "zinbreg() (default settings, analytic") /
  med("bioChemists_ZINB", "zeroinfl() (default")
ratio_nm <- med("NMES1988_ZINB", "zinbreg() (default settings, analytic") /
  med("NMES1988_ZINB", "zeroinfl() (default")
p <- if (!is.null(saved)) saved$provenance
zinb_pairs <- Filter(function(x) x$model == "ZINB", pairs)
em_iter <- vapply(zinb_pairs, function(x) x$ours$fit$iter, 1L)
bfgs <- vapply(zinb_pairs, function(x) {
  as.integer(x$ref$fit$optim$counts[["gradient"]])
}, 1L)
names(em_iter) <- names(bfgs) <- vapply(zinb_pairs, `[[`, "", "spec_id")
```

The NB fits take a fraction of a second with either implementation. Our
ZINB fits are slower than `zeroinfl()` (about `r round(ratio_bc)` times on
bioChemists and `r round(ratio_nm)` times on NMES1988, against its default
settings). This is expected and was not a goal. EM improves the
likelihood by a roughly fixed fraction per iteration (linear convergence),
so it needs many iterations (here `r em_iter[["bioChemists_ZINB"]]` on
bioChemists and `r em_iter[["NMES1988_ZINB"]]` on NMES1988), each of which
runs complete IRLS fits of both parts and evaluates `dnbinom()` for every
observation, and `zinbreg()` keeps iterating until the gradient check
passes. `zeroinfl()` instead runs a quasi-Newton (BFGS) search on all
parameters at once, which needed `r bfgs[["bioChemists_ZINB"]]` and
`r bfgs[["NMES1988_ZINB"]]` gradient evaluations here (with its tight
settings).
Timings depend on the machine and its load, so only their order of
magnitude matters.

`r if (!is.null(p)) sprintf("The timings were measured on %s (%s, %s cores) under %s, with MASS %s, pscl %s and bench %s, on %s, for the package code of commit %s (code fingerprint %s; provenance %s).", p$os, p$cpu, p$cores, p$r_version, p$versions[['MASS']], p$versions[['pscl']], p$versions[['bench']], substr(p$date, 1, 10), substr(p$git_commit, 1, 7), p$fingerprint_installed, p$status) else ""`
`r if (!is.null(prov_check)) (if (prov_check$status == "matches") prov_check$message else paste0("**", prov_check$message, "**")) else ""`

Additional comparisons that are not part of the requirements (the standard
errors of theta and log(theta), the ZINB fits with the numeric Hessian, and
the full validity checks) are in the supplementary benchmark article on the
package website.
